spans.s:
Ukhā is the regular word or a ‘cooking pot,’ usually mentioned in connexion with sacrifice, from the Rigveda onwards. It was made of clay (mṛṇ-mayī). See also sthālī.
Foot notes i. 162, 13. 15; iii. 53, 22; Av. xii. 3, 23; taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 1, 6, 3, etc.
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xi. 59; Taitdrīya Saṃhitā, iv. 1, 5, 4.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 253, 271.
